- Get your two most senior coaches in a room for 90 mins. Have them list every service/program members currently ask for or use (memberships tiers, classes, PT, nutrition coaching, challenges, etc.). You'll find inconsistencies — different coaches pricing things differently or offering things others don't. This mess is costing you money.

**Create two separate docs, not one**

**Lock in your pricing architecture TODAY**
- Don't overthink this. Pick your core offer (monthly membership), then 2-3 add-ons max (PT package, nutrition addon, challenge entry). ## REVENUE — INCREASE

• **Churn spike in May (12.8%) killed growth; now stabilised but still elevated.** Last 3 months average 6.6% vs prior 3-month 7.8% — improvement, but target 3–4% (you hit it twice). Sep headcount (165) is your highest; **focus Sep–Oct on retention mechanics**: exit-interview data, class-booking friction, peak-time capacity issues. At 165 members, losing 6% monthly = 10 members gone; at £124 Rev/member that's £1,240 monthly churn leakage.

• **Rev/member collapsed Aug (£106) despite 153 active members.** This signals low engagement or payment lag. Sep bounced to £133 — **audit Aug payment timing on GoCardless/Stripe; flag any failed direct debits**. If genuine engagement drop, run a "August slump" analysis: were classes cancelled, staff away, summer holidays? Plan counter-programming (outdoor classes, August challenge, loyalty bonus) for 2027.

• **Last 3 months revenue averaging £19,313 vs prior 3 months £16,032 = +20% YoY trajectory.** You're growing. Next lever: **upsell PT/1-on-1 coaching** (marginal cost near zero if staff-led); **launch class packs or 10-class bundles at 15% premium** (lock cash early, reduce churn psychology). Current membership model isn't extracting enough from 165 members — target £150+ Rev/member by Q1 2027.

---

## EXPENSES — REDUCE

• **No P&L visibility given.** Request a full monthly expense breakdown (payroll, rent post-relocation, utilities, payment processing fees, supplies). **Flag this immediately to your accountant.** Until you know COGS % and overhead split, you're flying blind. Assume: payroll ~50–60%, rent ~20–25%, payment processing ~2–3% of revenue. If processing fees are higher than 2.4%, **renegotiate Stripe/GoCardless terms — your volume (£22k/month) qualifies for better rates**.

• **Post-relocation rent likely higher.** Bigger studio = better capacity (you went 118→165 members) but payback period matters. **Calculate break-even: new rent vs old, divided by (new member revenue − old).** If rent jumped £2k/month, you need 16–20 new paying members to offset.
